The primary template definition (Keplerian fallback) is provided by default_property_getters.hpp, which celestial_bodies.hpp includes after all planet headers.

Used for bodies that have orbital element parameters but no Chebyshev ephemeris specialisation (e.g. Phobos, Deimos, small moons). The result is expressed in the parent-body ICRF frame derived from the body's parent origin.
Bodies WITH an explicit get_position_at specialisation (e.g. Earth, Jupiter when ephemeris is enabled) use that specialisation in preference to this primary template.

briefdescription.para: Keplerian fallback for get_acceleration_at.

detaileddescription.para: See get_position_at for usage notes.

briefdescription.para: Get the Keplerian elements of a celestial body at a specific date using a linear approximation.

detaileddescription.para: This uses the JPL approximate-positions algorithm: https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/celestial_bodies/approx_pos.html

Bodies that have get_linear_expansion_coefficients specialised use the full perturbation-corrected mean anomaly. All other bodies fall back to the default zero-coefficient implementation (Me = L - w).

parameterdescription.para: The date at which to compute the elements.

simplesect.para: Keplerian The approximate Keplerian elements at the given date.

briefdescription.para: Get the linear expansion coefficients for the celestial body's mean anomaly correction.

detaileddescription.para: Default implementation returns zero coefficients (no perturbation terms), which reduces to Me = L - w. Specialise for bodies that need it (e.g. outer planets).

simplesect.para: CoefficientPack A tuple containing (B, C, S, F) coefficients.

briefdescription.para: Compute the equivalent of Greenwich Sidereal Time for an arbitrary celestial body.

detaileddescription.para: Computes the accumulated rotation angle of the body's prime meridian relative to its inertial reference direction since J2000, using the body's rotation rate.

briefdescription.para: Finds the closest common ancestor of the given celestial bodies.

0 planets → only moons, check if they share a parent, else SolarSystemBarycenter.
